Was FUN_140005e60 (undefined; function created by hf ghidra-miner 2026-10-20). Per-tick aircraft attack run: ballistic lead check, fire or retire.
Algorithm:
- requires a target body (+0x158) with the 0x2f flag, a live +0x128 link and aim error +0x98 == 0.
- when the target is inside the band 50..800 + half its length, predicts the hit with Ballistics_PredictHit after offsetting by the profile wind (+0xac).
- small deviation tightens the stored aim error +0x90 and nudges +0xcc; a large deviation fires through MakeGlobal_ using the ammo-list entry from +0x120, then logs "STATE_RETIREMENT_AFTER_ATTACK" and moves state +400 to 4 (or 7 when the target is gone).
Parameters: rcx = aircraft logic; rdx = float[2] target position pair.
Returns: void.

Body_HasOid — tests whether a Body's m_oid string has been filled in.

Algorithm: returns (*(int*)(this+0x190) != 0). +0x190 is the first field of m_oid, an MSVC std::string (data-or-SSO buffer, length at +0x1a0, capacity at +0x1a8; see structures.md Body table). For an SSO string this reads the first four characters, so the result is false only when all four bytes are zero; for a heap-allocated string it reads the data pointer and is always true.

Parameters: this (Body*).
Returns: 1 when m_oid is non-empty / allocated, 0 when it looks empty.

Evidence: only caller is Projectile_DetonateOnImpulse at 0x14001d2e1, which calls it on the Body at projectile+0xa20 and skips the detonation branch when it returns 1.

Renamed from FUN_14002cdc0. Blast area damage: for each body in radius R = sqrt(E), damage = floor(5 x param x (1 - d/R)^2) with owner factor (0.66 enemy / 1.0 player), armoured-part and aircraft/missile multipliers; also adds the shell's incendiary value (+0x2e8) to a part's dose (+0x2f0). Calls Body_ApplyDamage.\n\nFriendly-fire note (2026-11-05): the 0.66/1.0 factor is only a player-ship damage scale, not a friend/foe filter; there is no side test. Called from Body_Explode and b2CListener_PreSolve. For same-side immunity, gate at entry 0x14002ce10 (after *param_6 = 0 at 0x14002ce0d; RCX = victim, RBP = exploder; early-out 0x14002d02d) and at the four direct Body_ApplyDamage sites in Body_Explode. See hf_notes/docs/findings/combat/friendly-fire-phasing.md.

RemoveLostAIShip (old name: rep_1400685c0_Get_Profile?)
RENAMED 2026-10-19: the old name was a 1.151-address placeholder plus a wrong "Get_Profile" guess (it only calls Get_Profile_ in passing). It is the end of ShipStatusCheck 0x14006ab70: called when an AI-controlled ship (creature+0xbd4 != 0) was judged lost.
[code, decompile read once, details approximate] Sets a timestamp (+0x17c*8 = GameClock), moves the ship's stored per-part counters (+0x804, cap 30 = 0x1e) to the other ships' parts in the list at +0x28a*8, bumps a profile counter (enigmaKey12) in some arcade cases, then calls the creature's vtable +0x48 (the "kill" slot BreakUpFrame also uses on parts) and sets +0x640 = -1. So this is what actually takes the ship out of the battle.
Open: what the +0x804 counters are (crew/evac/rescue stock?), what FUN_140079ed0 / FUN_140079790 / FUN_140293920 do. Notes: hf_ml/DESIGN_NOTES.md.

Was FUN_14006cb30. AI ship steering controller, called from aiShipDriver 0x1400739c0 (driver states 0 and 4). RESOLVED 2026-10-20: (1) The register scalar in the attitude gate is the hull moment of inertia I = Body_GetInertiaAboutOrigin(root) (result kept in a local, RBP+0xa0). Gate: Creature+0x180c turn_gate / I > 0.02 (0x140354674). (2) Target angle is 0 rad (XMM8 = 0.0, set by xorps at 0x14006cbc5): the AI keeps the hull level. e = wrap(0 - hull angle +0x138). P term: k = e x I / 20; bank-1 vector += k x h, bank-2 vector -= k x h, with h = (sin a, -cos a) (the same m +/- h construction as the player's Q/E, but with magnitude k instead of 1). No D term, no cap on k itself. (3) Translation: s = clamp(sqrt(dist + 0.1)/20, 0, 1) with dist to the target (+0xbf0/+0xbf4); F = [ (w x avoid + dir) x s x 100 x m - v x m ] / kk - (0, m x 9.82) with kk = 10 x m x 9.82 / (T1 + T2) where T1/T2 = bank thrust sums (+0x1664/+0x1668), m = total mass +0x15b8, w = Creature+0xc04, v = own velocity (+0x130/+0x134 of the root). So F is proportional to thrust capacity x (100 s dir - v) / (10 g) minus gravity compensation. (4) Each bank vector is clamped to 3 x its bank thrust sum, smoothed with a 5-slot ring average (+0xc1c..+0xc6c), then sent as cmd 100/0x65 (angle = atan2 of the smoothed vector, world frame) and 0x66/0x67 (angle the same, strength = |vector| / bank thrust sum, so up to 3.0 vs the player's 1.0 or 2.0 boost) to every part in the list +0x1330. Avoidance: AiShip_ScanObstacles fills the list at +0xd78; each obstacle adds weight ((10 - r)/10)^2, r = obstacle distance term / closing speed along its direction, zero for r > 10.

Creature_SumOffensiveScore

Offensive-share term of the Creature combat value (+0x15f8), computed once per
Creature::CalculateStats pass.

Algorithm: returns +0x15e8 + +0x15ec + +0x15f0 + +0x15f4. Those four counters
are accumulated by Creature_AccumulatePartStats (0x140071380):
  +0x15e8 - twice Stats+0xec of every part that has a weapon priority and a
            caliber (the gun damage/score term);
  +0x15ec - number of Zenith launchers (logic id 1 or 0x84, +0x848 == 0);
  +0x15f0 - number of bomb parts (m_category bit 21);
  +0x15f4 - number of aircraft parts (logic id 500).
CalculateStats adds the fuel term and 0.25 x battle TWR to this sum before the
final rating multiply (0x14007fcf0), so this helper is exactly the "how much
offense does the design carry" part.

Parameters: param_1 - Creature (0x1a50, 0x2f) with the +0x15e8 block filled.
Returns: float sum; 0 for an unarmed ship.

Effect vtable (0x140356a08) slot 18 - read the effect's projection-matrix constant.

Algorithm:
Copy the 16 floats at this+0xc0 .. this+0xfc into the caller's 64-byte output buffer. +0xc0 is the matrix that Effect_SetProjectionMatrix (slot 17, 0x140088830) builds and pushes through the matrix property at this+0xb8, so this is the matching getter.

Parameters:
this - Effect; param_2 - out pointer to 16 floats.

Returns:
param_2.

Effect vtable (0x140356a08) slot 16 - install a projection matrix supplied by the caller.

Algorithm:
Copy the caller's 16 floats into this+0xc0 .. this+0xfc, then tail-call Property_SetFloat16 (0x1400a00b0) on the matrix property stored at this+0xb8, which compares the block with the current value, notifies the owner through its vtable +0x28 and writes it back.

Parameters:
this - Effect; param_2 - pointer to 16 floats.

Returns:
nothing (tail call).

Editor click-mode handler: returns 0 unless the editor flag 0x1403EF368 is set, otherwise runs the part-attach routine 0x1400C12A0 and returns 1. That routine (this is its only caller) collects Body.slots of the editor bodies, filters Slot.is_master/is_slave (0x84/0x85), pairs slots whose Slot.m_type mask (0xB8) nests, tests the pair distance, snaps both bodies with setXposYpos and stores the pair in 0x1403EF380/0x1403EF388. Called from Input_HandleMouseMove 0x140187260 (0x140187572); neighbours are Editor_HandleClickMode5 0x1400BC580 and Editor_HandleZoomWheel 0x1400BC5E0. 'Attach' is the reading of 0x1400C12A0; the flag 0x1403EF368 is unnamed.

Merges one aircraft group into another when both belong to the same side.

Algorithm:
    Compares the side from virtual +0x178; only equal sides are merged. Copies the source group ship list, reloads ammo, resets each source ship state (+0x1f0 = 2, clears links/timers), recalculates the ship and group stats through Escadra_RecalculateShipStats, moves the surviving ships into the destination group, and finally refreshes the LOADOUT_LIST / CRAFT_UNREADY_LIST GUI.

Parameters:
    param_1 - destination aircraft group
    param_2 - source aircraft group

Returns:
    nothing.

Builds the curved manoeuvre path of a fleet from its current position to a destination.

Algorithm:
    Clears the path list at +0x318, derives the direction and length to param_2, then iteratively halves the turn step until the swept angle times the turn radius fits the allowed turn budget (fuel/speed dependent). Emits the intermediate path points as 0x18-byte list nodes at the computed offsets and stops when the remaining angle is consumed.

Parameters:
    param_1 - fleet / moving object (position +0x150/+0x154, heading, speed)
    param_2 - packed destination (x in low dword, y in high dword)

Returns:
    nothing.

Tests whether an object is not parented under a Body/Frame/Creature.

Algorithm: returns true when the master pointer at +0x88 is null, else compares the master's class code at +0x28 with 7. Class code 7 is Node (Creature 47, Body 15, Frame 31, Node 7), so the true result means "no master, or the master is a plain Node", i.e. a top-level body rather than a part.
Parameters: this - Node/Body object.
Returns: 1 for a top-level/unanchored object, else 0.

vcruntime GS + SEH exception handler (stock MSVC __GSHandlerCheck).

Algorithm:
    Calls __GSHandlerCheckCommon(pExcept, pRN, pContext, pDC) to check the GS cookie
    stored in the function's GS handler data, then returns 1 (ExceptionContinueSearch)
    so the rest of the handler chain runs.

Parameters:
    param_1 - EXCEPTION_RECORD* (pExcept).
    param_2 - EHRegistrationNode* (pRN).
    param_3 - CONTEXT* (pContext).
    param_4 - DispatcherContext* (pDC); its GSHandlerData holds the cookie.

Returns:
    1 (ExceptionContinueSearch).

Scalar-to-4-lane sine shim used by b2TimeOfImpact.

Algorithm: SHUFPS XMM0,XMM1,0 broadcasts lane 0, ADDPS with 0.0 from 0x140379020, then tail-jumps to sinf4 (0x140334de0). 13 bytes.
Parameters: XMM0 = scalar float.
Returns: XMM0 = sinf4 of the broadcast value.

Constructor for the std::bad_alloc exception object used by the new-handler path.

Algorithm:
    Sets the exception's two pointer fields (this+8 message pointer, this+0x10 length = 0), points this+8 at the literal "bad allocation" and installs the std::exception vtable 0x1403522b8 (the pointer at 0x1403522b8 is `__std_exception_destroy`). Returns this. Its only job is to give `badAllocationException` 0x140334e70 a ready-made object.

Parameters:
    param_1 - storage for the std::bad_alloc object.

Returns:
    param_1.

Startup SEH filter that forwards the exception to _seh_filter_exe.

Algorithm:
    Unpacks the exception-pointers argument into (ExceptionCode, ExceptionPointers) and calls the CRT's _seh_filter_exe with them. Used as the __except filter of mainCRTStartup's __try around the whole initialise/initterm/Main/exit sequence; the handler body is empty.

Parameters:
    param_1 - _EXCEPTION_POINTERS* supplied by the unwinder.

Returns:
    _seh_filter_exe's disposition.
